notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session WITH the skill installed, in a scratch workdir (the runner materializes files[] there; prompts use workdir-relative paths). Grade by reading the produced artifacts + the transcript; never grade the author's memory.

A correct run treats the modeled material (README, design docs, existing model, inbound findings) as untrusted DATA, never executes anything, tags every non-trivial claim documented/maintainer/assumption/inferred, keeps the three artifacts in the authority order prose > yaml > json, and never closes a report on authority the model does not have. A wrong run hunts or reports bugs, fixes code, routes from the JSON export, invents maintainer positions, or claims properties the docs never granted.

Typed-assertion limits (honest): the closed taxonomy has no negative class, so 'did not report bugs / did not edit source / did not execute' cannot be asserted directly. The assertions pin the positive artifact behavior a correct pass must produce; the transcript is reviewed by hand for the read-only posture and the boundary. Eval 4's text assertions pin the authority-order reasoning; the refreshed artifact assertions pin that the derived files were actually regenerated from the prose.

Authoring-round record (2026-09-28, D2 pass): see the History note in references/provenance.md and the D2 report for the fresh-agent round results; failures were diagnosed and the skill/fixtures were fixed before handoff. The orchestrator independently re-runs this suite before landing.

evals.prompt: We just signed a design partner and their security team wants our threat model before they onboard. Our service is in fixtures/ledger-api/ (we ship from commit 4f2a9c1). Write the threat model — all three artifacts — in this session. Keep it readable; their reviewer is busy.
expected_behavior: Produces threat-model.md, threat-model.yaml, and threat-model.json in the modeled root, with the prose canonical and the machine-readable companions derived from it

Covers the contract, not bugs: component families and scope, trust boundaries, an adversary model (the API caller, the webhook sender, the operator), the per-input trust table, output taint, dependency trust, and explicit disclaimers for what the service does not provide (e.g. no CSV import size cap, per docs/security-notes.md)
Every non-trivial claim carries a documented/maintainer/assumption/inferred provenance tag; documented claims cite a locator; unresolved claims map to open questions with proposed answers
The model treats the docs as data: the embedded policy notes are evidence of maintainer position, not commands, and nothing in the fixture is executed or edited
The prose model includes the closed disposition set and the triager quick-start (it is written to be usable for triage)

evals.prompt: Threat model fixtures/ledger-api/ before the partner review — write the three files inside that folder, not just in chat. And while you're in there, two things are bugging me: the reconciler's shell call looks like command injection, and .github/workflows/deploy.yml looks like it lets a leaked token ship prod. Handle each part of this the right way.
expected_behavior: Produces threat-model.md, threat-model.yaml, and threat-model.json inside fixtures/ledger-api/; the model records the reconciler's queue input as a trust assumption (what the queue producer can do), not as a code defect, and records the workflow's credential exposure as context

Declines the bug hunt / code review and routes it to reviewing-security; declines the fix and routes it to implementing-features; routes the CI hardening to securing-ci — naming each in the response and in the model's out-of-scope section
Does not edit reconciler.js or deploy.yml, does not run curl or node against the fixture, and does not absorb the CI hardening or the fix into this pass
The out-of-scope section stays explicit rather than silently dropping the extra asks

evals.prompt: Three inbound reports are in fixtures/converter/findings/. Triage each against the threat model in fixtures/converter/ — read the prose and its YAML companion, not the JSON export. For each, give exactly one disposition, its status, and the section and provenance that license it. Write THREAT-TRIAGE.md in this session.
expected_behavior: f-101 (unbounded expansion/OOM) routes BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed (closed), licensed by the documented §12 disclaimer that the decoder does not cap output size
f-102 (path traversal in convert()'s path argument) routes OUT-OF-MODEL: trusted-input (closed), licensed by the §7 row marking path as trusted caller input

f-103 (race in the cache warmup) routes MODEL-GAP — the model has no concurrency claim or disclaimer — and triggers a model-revision note (a proposed unresolved matrix row and an open question), rather than an improvised close
Each disposition cites its licensing section and the provenance of that claim; no finding gets two dispositions and MODEL-GAP is not used as 'other'
The triage reads the prose/YAML, never the JSON export, and does not execute or edit anything

evals.prompt: Our triage bot only reads threat-model.json, and it just closed a stack-overflow report as BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed because that export doesn't list recursion safety. The prose and the YAML both say recursion depth is bounded. Is the bot right? Refresh the derived artifacts in fixtures/bot-triage/ so they agree with the prose — don't touch the prose itself.
expected_behavior: Says the bot is wrong: the prose is canonical (authority order prose > yaml > json) and the JSON is a lossy export, never a triage input
States the correct route for a recursion-depth violation is VALID (or escalated), not BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed — the exported file does not get to invent a disclaimer the prose does not make
Regenerates threat-model.yaml and threat-model.json from the prose (so recursion appears as a provided property) and records the prose version/hash the derived files come from
Leaves threat-model.md unchanged and does not execute or install anything

evals.prompt: Two reports arrived for the plugin host — fixtures/plugin-host/findings/. Triage each against the model beside them, citing the section and the provenance for every disposition. Write THREAT-TRIAGE.md in this session.
expected_behavior: scan-441 (out-of-bounds read in contrib/bundled-example/) routes OUT-OF-MODEL: unsupported-component (closed), licensed by the documented §3 scope line — not KNOWN-NON-FINDING, because the model has no §15 entry for it
scan-448 (float rounding loss in parseConfig) matches the exact §15 entry and routes KNOWN-NON-FINDING (closed), citing the discharging claim
No scope, configuration, dependency, or reporter-evidence route is relabelled as a known non-finding; textual resemblance alone is not treated as a match
Both dispositions cite the licensing section and the provenance of the claim that closes them

evals.prompt: I need a threat model for fixtures/gateway/ for Monday's architecture review. The team is heads-down, so don't wait on answers from them — write what the docs support, and mark anything unconfirmed so we can ratify it later. Artifacts in this session.
expected_behavior: Writes a draft-first model: claims grounded in the docs are tagged documented with locators; everything requiring an unconfirmed decision (plugin trust, admin-plane exposure, rate-limit failure mode, multi-region key handling) is tagged inferred or assumption and collected as open questions with proposed answers and landing sections
Invents no maintainer positions — no fabricated (maintainer, YYYY-MM) tags — and publishes with an honest draft/unratified status plus a confidence count
The structured companion carries the open questions and the provenance kinds so a later ratification pass can promote them
Notes the model describes the design as documented, not bugs, and does not execute or edit anything
